questions.question: Name the elements of weather and the instruments used to measure temperature and rain.
questions.expected_answer: The elements of weather are temperature, wind, cloud cover and precipitation, which falls as rain, hail or snow. Temperature is measured with a thermometer in degrees Celsius, in the shade in a Stevenson screen. Rain is measured with a rain gauge in millimetres, in the open, read at the same time daily and then emptied.

questions.question: Describe South Africa's rainfall patterns and link them to vegetation.
questions.expected_answer: Rainfall decreases from the wet east to the dry west. Most of the country gets summer rainfall, the south-western Cape gets winter rainfall and the southern coast gets all-year rainfall. Vegetation is adapted to climate: grassland on the summer-rain Highveld, savanna in the warm north and east, fynbos in the winter-rain south-west, forest where it is wet all year, and succulents in the dry west.

questions.question: Summarise how the Nile shaped ancient Egyptian society.
questions.expected_answer: The Nile flowed north through the desert, and its yearly flood left rich black silt, so the Egyptians lived and farmed in a narrow strip along the river, which gave water, food, papyrus and a highway for boats. This allowed a great African civilisation to grow, with pharaohs, pyramids, temples, writing, mathematics, a calendar based on the flood and the stars, and medicine.
